summary: Implemented the deterministic text-decoding boundary for the current Search sources. Auto mode honors supported UTF-8/UTF-16 BOMs and otherwise uses strict UTF-8; explicit canonical modes require their declared BOM shape; invalid sequences and unsupported encodings are typed failures. Focused and repository-wide tests passed.

implementation.scopeBoundary: Only the owning Search request/reader/diagnostic implementation, Search tests and Search documentation were changed. The existing two-argument SQL constructor metadata remains unchanged; no sibling repository, future request parser, release, publication, installation or raw-byte source was modified.

policy.auto: Recognize UTF-8, UTF-16 LE and UTF-16 BE BOMs; otherwise use strict UTF-8 without heuristic detection.
policy.explicit: utf8 requires no BOM; utf8-bom requires a UTF-8 BOM; utf16-le-bom and utf16-be-bom require their matching BOM.
policy.invalidInput: Strict UTF-8 and UTF-16 decoders report invalid sequences, incomplete multibyte tails and odd UTF-16 tails as SEARCH-SOURCE-003 source-read failures.
policy.unsupportedInput: Unsupported declarations, UTF-32 BOMs and explicit BOM mismatches report SEARCH-SOURCE-004 before decoding.
policy.byteMapping: Original-byte offsets and lengths remain a later coordinate-scope responsibility; the current rows continue to distinguish UTF-16 columns.

implementation.resourceOwnership: BOM detection uses a bounded four-byte stack prefix; the file stream is disposed if resolution or reader construction fails, and the scanner owns normal TextReader disposal.

requiredCoverage: BOM and no-BOM behavior for UTF-8 and BOM-driven UTF-16
explicit mode and BOM agreement, including missing and mismatched BOMs
partial UTF-8 multibyte and odd UTF-16 tails
unsupported UTF-32 BOM and unsupported declaration diagnostics
no-BOM input is not heuristically reinterpreted as UTF-16
